cards.text: Jeremiah is a prophet, and he's been carrying the LORD's hard warning to Judah: they broke His covenant (Jeremiah 11:10). Now Jeremiah talks to the LORD about something personal. The LORD informed him, so he knew, and showed him what certain people had been doing.

cards.question: Before the LORD showed him, what does Jeremiah say he was like?

answers.text: A gentle lamb led to slaughter

cards.text: Here's what certain people had plotted against him: 'Let us destroy the tree with its fruit; let us cut him off from the land of the living, that his name may be remembered no more.'

cards.question: Jeremiah says he did not know about the plot against him.

cards.text: So Jeremiah turns to the LORD of Hosts, who judges righteously and examines the heart and mind. Friend, if somebody plotted against ME, I'd be hiding behind the ovens with my apron over my face.

cards.question: Jeremiah tells the LORD he'll get back at the plotters himself.
Jeremiah has committed his cause to the LORD. He asks the LORD of Hosts to let him see His ___ upon them.

cards.text: Then the LORD names who is seeking Jeremiah's life: the people of Anathoth, a town in the land of Benjamin. And Anathoth is where Jeremiah comes from (Jeremiah 1:1).

cards.question: What do the people of Anathoth tell Jeremiah he must not do?

answers.text: Prophesy in the name of the LORD

cards.text: And if he keeps it up, they tell him, '…you will die by our hand.' I think this one hurts, friend.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts speaks about the people of Anathoth. What does He say He will do to them?

cards.text: Their young men will die by the sword, the LORD says, and their sons and daughters by famine. He will bring disaster on the people of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.

cards.question: The LORD says a remnant of the people of Anathoth will be left.

cards.text: Jeremiah keeps talking to the LORD: 'Righteous are You, O LORD, when I plead before You.' Then comes 'Yet,' and I know that move, friend, because I tell my oven it's doing GREAT right before I ask why my cookies came out like hockey pucks.

cards.question: Jeremiah wants to contend with the LORD about His judgments. He asks why the way of the ___ prospers.

cards.text: Jeremiah says the LORD planted the wicked, and they've taken root, grown and produced fruit. Fruit talk again, and this time it's the wicked who produce it.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the wicked never talk about the LORD.
The LORD is always on the lips of the wicked. What does Jeremiah say about their hearts?

cards.text: Then Jeremiah says, 'But You know me, O LORD; You see me and test my heart toward You.'

cards.question: Jeremiah says the LORD tests his heart. What does he ask the LORD to do with the wicked?

answers.text: Drag them away like sheep to slaughter
Give them one more year to change
Send them off to a far country

cards.text: Earlier, Jeremiah was like a gentle lamb led to slaughter. Now he wants the wicked dragged off like sheep, and he asks how long the land will mourn and the grass of every field be withered.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the animals and birds have been swept away because of the evil of the land's residents.

cards.text: The people have been saying, 'He cannot see what our end will be.' Then an answer comes to Jeremiah, and it starts with a picture of a race.

cards.question: In the race picture, men on foot have worn Jeremiah out. What faster racers does the picture bring up next?

cards.text: Then a second picture, about the Jordan River: 'If you stumble in a peaceful land, how will you do in the thickets of the Jordan?' Friend, I'm a stamper on a gold base, so put me in a race with horses and they'll be home ASLEEP before I clear the first hill.

cards.question: Jeremiah is told that even his ___, his own father's household, have betrayed him.
Jeremiah is told to trust his father's household when they speak well of him.
